text:
jamie-chen: Quick question — I'll start parental leave 2026-06-01 and plan to spend ~3 months in Portugal while on leave. Will payroll tax withholding change if I'm physically abroad? Do I need to file additional paperwork or notify anyone?

raj-payroll: Short answer: maybe. If you're remaining on Redwood's US payroll and not doing paid work for a foreign employer, payroll typically continues as usual, but tax residency rules can affect withholding + reporting. We need an international work notification so payroll and benefits can review.

emily-hr: To add — your benefits (medical, parental pay, etc.) continue per policy while on approved leave. Tax outcomes are separate from benefits eligibility. Please don't assume no tax change until payroll confirms. :+1:

jamie-chen: Thanks — where's the form? Anything I should include besides dates and country?

raj-payroll: Use the "International Work / Leave Location" form: https://redwood.internal/hr/payroll/international-work (or submit via the People Ops portal). Include start/end dates, city/country, and whether you'll be doing any client-facing/paid work while abroad. If you plan to take any short consulting gigs while away, tell us — that changes the rules.

liam-payroll-bot: Thanks! Jamie's submission received (ID: INT-2026-0543). Payroll will triage and follow up within 3 business days.

jamie-chen: Do I need to upload passport/visa scans?

emily-hr: Not for initial notification. If payroll/intl HR need documentation to determine tax residency or to set up local payroll, we'll request specific docs. For now just the dates, country, and statement of whether you'll undertake compensated work.

raj-payroll: A few practical notes:
- If you stay <90 days and remain on US payroll doing no remote paid work for a foreign entity, usually withholding stays the same.
- If you exceed local statutory thresholds (e.g., 183-day tests) or do paid work for a foreign client/employer, we may need to engage our global mobility / tax advisor and potentially run local payroll or change withholding.
- For paid leave (company parental pay), we'll continue gross payments but tax withholdings might differ — we'll show any expected changes before the first paycheck while you're abroad.

jamie-chen: Got it. What about 401(k) and HSA contributions while on leave?

raj-payroll: 401(k): If payroll is still on the US payroll and you're receiving pay, pre-tax contributions typically continue. If you go unpaid (unpaid leave) contributions pause. HSA eligibility depends on your medical coverage status — if coverage continues, you remain eligible. We'll confirm based on your specific leave pay status.

emily-hr: Action items:
1) Jamie: submit the international work notification (if not already done).
2) Payroll: triage and confirm any withholding changes + impact to 401k/HSA.
3) HR: note benefits coverage stays in place; escalate to global mobility if payroll flags residency concerns.

jamie-chen: Submitted the form just now. Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.

liam-payroll-bot: Payroll assigned to raj-payroll for INT-2026-0543. Expect a DM with next steps and any doc requests.

raj-payroll: We'll follow up by end of day tomorrow with what (if anything) will change on your first leave paycheck. If anything urgent comes up, ping me directly.
